result.title: EvoWeb: A Benchmark for Coding Agents on Evolving Web Applications
result.summary: Web application development often proceeds through successive requests that extend an existing implementation. Yet web-generation benchmarks primarily evaluate development toward fixed specifications. We introduce EvoWeb, a novel benchmark comprising 320 cumulative requests over 32 web applications, grounded in real-world product features and structured by functional dependency graphs. Agents iteratively modify a persistent codebase, while a multimodal web agent tests each intermediate application in a live browser, assessing newly requested functionality, cross-request integration, and previously requested functionality. To characterize reliability throughout development, we integrate trajectory performance across user-tolerance thresholds rather than impose a fixed stopping criterion. Experiments across open- and closed-source frontier models show that EvoWeb reveals clear performance differences between models, with cross-request integration emerging as a key challenge. Further analysis shows that later requests with deeper or more numerous dependencies are solved less accurately, while runtime errors become more frequent over successive requests. EvoWeb provides a testbed for evaluating and improving coding agents in long-horizon, multi-request development.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EvoWeb，一个针对渐进式 Web 应用开发的 coding agent 基准：320 个累积请求、32 个应用，用功能依赖图组织，并由多模态 web agent 在真实浏览器中逐轮测试新功能、跨请求集成与旧功能。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽含多模态浏览器测试与长时程累积请求，但研究对象是代码修改与端到端功能可靠性，不涉及 VLM 内部推理状态、视觉证据筛选或 latent 生成，未发现可迁移到 LVR 的具体线索。
